newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai 1997 water usage seen at record high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai 1997 water usage seen at record high.

text.p: Water consumption in Shanghai, China's biggest and fastest growing city, will reach a record 13 billion cubic metres (17 billion cubic yards) in 1997, up from 10.7 billion cubic metres (14 billion cubic yards) in 1990, the Liberation Daily said on Sunday.
Water usage in Shanghai has risen by an average of 2.9 percent a year since 1985, it said.
Industrial water usage had surged 30 percent year-on-year since 1985, while daily residential water usage was up 5.2 percent year-on-year, it said.
Water shortages have forced Shanghai to borrow water from neighbouring Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces twice during the past five years, it said.

Water supply to China's rural areas falls short of need by 30 billion cubic metres (39 billion cubic yards) per year, and in the cities by six billion cubic metres (7.8 billion cubic yards), the Business News said.
It said that most of China's major water sources are severely polluted, but gave no further details.
